Dish 1 · 1 serve

Crispy-Skin Barramundi

Brown-Rice Prawn Risotto

Charred corn, peas, baby spinach, heirloom tomato, lemon and basil oil.

Ingredients & method — Crispy-Skin Barramundi

Ingredients (1 serve)

Barramundi
Humpty Doo barramundi fillet (skin on)160–180 g
Olive oil10 ml
Salt2 g
Black pepper1 g
Brown-Rice Risotto
Cooked brown rice (pre-cooked)120–140 g
Prawns (diced)2 each (40 g)
Charred corn kernels30 g
Peas20–25 g
Baby spinach15 g
Heirloom cherry tomatoes2 each (30 g)
Red onion (finely diced)15 g
Garlic (minced)5 g
Parmesan (grated)15 g
Butter15 g
Chicken or vegetable stock (hot)100–150 ml
Salt and black pepperTo taste
Finishing
Lemon (zest and juice)½ lemon
Basil oil5 ml
Micro herbsTo garnish

Method

  1. Season barramundi with salt and pepper.
  2. Cook skin-side down in a hot pan with oil until crispy, then finish in the oven or flip to cook through. Rest.
  3. In a pan, sweat onion and garlic. Add cooked brown rice and hot stock; bring to the right consistency.
  4. Add prawns, corn, peas and spinach. Finish with butter and Parmesan. Season to taste.
  5. Halve and blister the cherry tomatoes.
  6. Plate the risotto, top with barramundi skin-side up and arrange tomatoes. Finish with lemon, basil oil and micro herbs. Keep oil off the crisp skin.

Key points

  • Use pre-cooked brown rice to save time.
  • Keep the risotto glossy and loose, not dry.
  • Do not overcook the fish.

Dish 2 · 1 serve

Eye Fillet

Caramelised-Onion Potato Croquette

Mushroom ragout, charred broccolini, roasted garlic-Parmesan butter and herb oil.

Ingredients & method — Eye Fillet

Ingredients (1 serve)

Eye Fillet
Eye fillet steak180 g
Olive oil10 ml
Salt2 g
Black pepper1 g
Caramelised-Onion Potato Croquette
Mashed potato (cold)125 g
Caramelised onion (for the centre)20 g
Egg yolk1 each
Plain flour15 g
Beaten egg (for crumbing)As needed
Breadcrumbs30 g
Salt and pepperTo taste
OilFor frying
Mushroom Ragout
Mixed mushrooms (sliced)100 g
Shallot (finely diced)15 g
Garlic (minced)5 g
Butter10 g
Cream30 ml
Thyme (if available)1 g
Salt and black pepperTo taste
Roasted Garlic-Parmesan Butter
Unsalted butter (softened)25 g
Roasted garlic (minced)5 g
Parmesan (grated)5 g
Basil (finely chopped)2 g
Lemon zest1 g
Salt and pepperTo taste
Charred Broccolini
Broccolini3–4 stems (60 g)
Olive oil5 ml
Salt and pepperTo taste
Jus (optional)
Beef or red-wine jus30 ml
Finishing
Herb oil5 ml
Micro herbsTo garnish

Method

  1. Mix cold mash with egg yolk and seasoning. Form a cylinder around the caramelised-onion centre. Coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, then chill. Fry until golden and crisp.
  2. Cook mushrooms, shallot and garlic in butter. Add cream, thyme and seasoning. Reduce to a ragout.
  3. Season eye fillet and sear in a hot pan to the desired doneness. Rest.
  4. Char broccolini in a hot pan with oil and season.
  5. Mix the roasted garlic-Parmesan butter ingredients, chill and slice a medallion.
  6. Plate the mushroom ragout and place the steak on top with the butter. Add the croquette and broccolini. Finish with herb oil, micro herbs and jus if using.

Key points

  • Keep the croquette cold before frying for a crisp exterior.
  • Keep the caramelised onion inside the croquette.
  • Rest the steak properly.
  • Keep mushroom ragout rich but not too wet.
  • Add the butter just before serving.
